A.
This is an appeal by The Commissioner General of Inland
Revenue (Hereinafter sometimes referred to as CGIR/
Appellant) from the determination of the Tax Appeals
Commission dated 30.08.2019 made in TAC appeal no.
TAC/IT/037/2015. The Respondent is VARNERS LANKA LAW
OFFICE (Hereinafter sometimes referred to as Taxpayer,
The Respondent).
The Appellant being dissatisfied with the Determination of Tax
Appeal Commission (Hereinafter sometimes referred to as
TAC) requested for an appeal by a case stated for the opinion of
the Court of Appeal by their communication dated 24.09.2019.
B.
On 03.07.2026, both parties concluded the argument. It is
found that the Appellant has furnished written submissions on

C.
In the case stated dated 15.10.2019 following questions were
raised for the opinion of the Court of Appeal:-
1. Whether Natural Justice Principles have been violated at
the Stage of the appeal heard by the Commissioner
General of Inland Revenue?
2. Whether the TAC has erred in law that coming into
conclusion without considering the substantive issues?
The tax payer submits its income tax return for the taxable
periods 2010/2011 and 2011/2012. The claim was rejected by
the Assessor and that the Tax Payer was not entitled for
exemption under section 13 (ddd) for the relevant taxable
periods. The return is not accepted and issued an assessment
disallowing some of the exemptions and expenses claimed.
QUESTIONS OF LAW
TAX RETURN
ANALYSIS
Judgment CA Tax No. 38/2019 Page 5|10
Having aggrieved by the said Assessments, the tax payer made
an appeal to the CGIR. The Tax Payer made the same agitation
before the CGIR. CGIR by his determination dated 29.09.2015
determined the appeal by confirming the assessments
The tax payer having not satisfied with the determination of the
CGIR, made an appeal to the TAC. In the appeal before the TAC
the tax payer raised the same issues. After hearing the Appeal,
the Tax Appeals Commission, by determination dated 30 August
2019, annulled the assessment previously confirmed by the
Commissioner General of Inland Revenue and allowed the
taxpayer’s appeal. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid determination of
the Tax Appeals Commission the Appellant, Commissioner General
of Inland Revenue, made an application by letter dated 24
September 2019 for a Stated Case, for the opinion of Court of
Appeal on the questions of law enumerated therein. In the case
stated, the Appellant has submit two issues for the opinion of the
Court of Appeal, that is whether the Natural Justice Principles have
been violated when the appeal was heard by CGIR and whether the
TAC can determine the appeal without considering the substantial
issues.
FIRST APPEAL
SECOND APPEAL
Judgment CA Tax No. 38/2019 Page 6|10
It is contended by the Respondent that, the two questions cannot
be raised in the case stated for the opinion of the Court of
Appeal since they are questions of fact and not questions of
law. The objections relates to the jurisdiction of the Court. It is
mandatory duty of the Court to consider the jurisdictional issue of
the earliest possible opportunity and clear the jurisdictional defects.
P. Beatrice perera Vs. The commissioner of National Housing
and 3 others 77 NLR 361
Kekul Kotuwage Don Aruna Chaminda Vs. Janashakthi
General Insurance Limited (SC/Appeal No. 134/2018)
We had the opportunity of hearing the full argument on the merits
of the matter. However, as the questions submitted in the case
stated for the opinion of the Court, turned as non questions of law,
the Court called for written submissions from the parties on the
jurisdictional issue. Although both parties tendered its written
submissions belatedly, the same did not deal with the jurisdictional
issue at all.
VITAL ISSUE
Judgment CA Tax No. 38/2019 Page 7|10
The Section 11 A (6) of the Tax Appeals Commission
Act No 23 of 2011 (as amended) is as follows;
“11 A (6) Any two or more Judges of the Court of
Appeal may hear and determine any question
of law arising on the stated case and may in
accordance with the decision of Court upon
such question, confirm, reduce, increase or
annul the assessment determined by the
Commission, or may remit the case to the
Commission with the opinion of the Court,
thereon. Where a case is so remitted by the
Court, the Commission shall revise”
“170 (1) – The decision of the Board shall be final:
Provided that either the Appellant or the
Commissioner General may make an application
requiring the Board to state a case on a question of
SECTION 11 OF TAC ACT
SECTION 170 OF THE IRA No. 10 of 2006
Judgment CA Tax No. 38/2019 Page 8|10
law for the opinion of the Court of Appeal. Such
application shall not be entertained unless it is
made in writing and delivered to the Secretary to
the Board, together with a fee of one thousand and
five hundred rupees, within one month of the date
on which the decision of the Board was notified in
writing to the Commissioner General or the
Appellant, as the case may be.
(6) Any two or more Judges of the Court of Appeal may
hear and determine any question of law arising on the
stated case and may in accordance with the decision of
Court upon such question, confirm, reduce, increase or
annul the assessment determined by the Board, or may
remit the case to the Board with the opinion of the
Judgment CA Tax No. 38/2019 Page 9|10
Court, thereon. Where a case is so remitted by the Court,
the Board shall revise the assessment in accordance
with the opinion of the Court.
Accordingly, the Court of Appeal may consider and determine any
Questions of Law arising on the stated case, upon which the
Court may confirm reduce, increase or annual the assessment.
Thus, it is clear that the Court of Appeal does not in any manner
have the jurisdiction to deal with the pure finding of fact of the
TAC. However, wrong analysis of the Question of fact is a Question
of Law.
In Collects Limited Vs. Bank Of Ceylon 2SLR 574, it has been
held that the improper analysis of fact is a Question of Law.
In this case before the Court, we do not have sufficient materials to
conclude that the TAC has come to an incorrect finding on this pure
question of fact. Therefore, the questions raised by the Appellant
will not amount to questions of law, granting jurisdiction to
become triable by this Court.
RESTRICTION
Judgment CA Tax No. 38/2019 Page 10|10
Question No 1 is in respect of observance of principle of natural
justice at the hearing before the CGIR. Question No 2 is in respect
of TAC’s conclusion on preliminary issue. There is not a point of law
involved in the two questions as those were framed. As the
questions raised in the case stated are not questions of law and as
per Section 11A of the TAC Act and Section 170 (1) proviso and 170
(6) of IRA No. 10 of 2006, this Court has no jurisdiction to try the
stated case.
D.
As analyzed above and as the two questions raised in the case
stated are not questions of law, this Court has no jurisdiction to try
the stated case and the same is REJECTED.
The Registrar is directed to forward a copy of the judgment to the
Tax appeal commission.
